question.text: The stopping potential for photoelectrons emitted from a surface illuminated by light of wavelength <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6630</mn><mo>Å</mo></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>42</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>. If the threshold frequency is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>13</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is (nearest integer): (Given, speed light <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>8</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.  Planck's constant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>63</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>34</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>)

solution.text:
We know that, KEmax=hf-ϕ=hcλ-ϕ

Or, hcλ-ϕ=eV0, where, ϕ=hνth and V0 is stopping potential.

So, threshold frequency is 

νth=cλ-eV0h

=3×10866330×10-10-1.6×10-19×0.426.63×10-34

=36.630×1015-1.6×0.426.63×1015

=101536.630-1.6×0.426.63=0.4524-0.1013

νth=35.11×1013
